scope: Read-only second review. No app source/test edits, builds, Simulator actions or protected parent changes.

compileFinding.original: Renderer lacked preparationID despite initializer and consume uses; immediately reported to root.
compileFinding.followup: Root added var preparationID: UUID? = nil. Exact one-line diff and corrected WorkoutView SHA417a4b27d7ae0ce1d1fa7f4dee440fadcea12d7a8c1b7a33a285edac61709e8f retained. No build result claimed by this review.

resolvedPriorFindings: Every preference record now carries request ID and consume requires all records to match the current request. New stale-snapshot test exercises a cancelled request against a new one.

Board readiness compares token, actual viewport, position, contacts and mode; hand readiness compares token, actual viewport, pose/finger configuration, side and reset token. A changed signature does not immediately inherit true readiness.

Workout pre-start content change cancels pending audio/visual arm, stops audio and reissues a fresh first-start request while routineStartedAt is nil. Main hand-choice and task controls remain available.

Actual raster branch emits a board record from positive finite viewport, and the parent always requires a board record. This removes inferred model/raster media and empty-preference fallback from the start condition.
Hands requirement matches portrait concrete-hold path or actual left/right cue policy. The existing Main single/pair/selected-side resolution is retained.

Initial countdown retains cue subtree via mountedCueCountdown and opacity; hidden wrappers now explicitly suppress hit testing and accessibility. Pair RealityView remains accessibilityHidden throughout.

cancelCountdown now resets the renderer gate; interruption, end, pending-toggle and disappearance cancellation remain connected. Skip/resume stay outside requestFirstStart initial branch; audio schedule and prescribed countdown/interval durations are unchanged.

remainingSourceRisk.finding: Preparation does not include model identity. synchronizedPreparation State belongs to outer BoardModelRealityView, while model .id is applied only to the inner RealityView. If a replacement loaded model reaches the same outer view without an observed intervening loading branch, unchanged token/viewport/selection could inherit prior scene readiness before replacement make. Ordinary loading UI replacement often resets this state, but the identity contract should not depend on that intermediate body being committed.
remainingSourceRisk.recommendation: Include ObjectIdentifier(model) in Preparation or otherwise scope the synchronization state to model identity. No actual runtime occurrence claimed.

runtimeBoundariesNotEstablishedBySourceR: Actual child preference propagation through BoardModelSurface parent preference, make-to-attachment timing and the initial loading-to-ready transition require hosted/runtime proof; aggregation tests alone do not cover them.
Opacity zero preserves SwiftUI structural identity but is not a guarantee of continuous GPU drawing or first displayed frame. The full first-Hang blank/color/hand gate remains unchanged.
Token and signature guard late scheduled assignments from producing true readiness for different current inputs. They are not a compositor or material-presentation guarantee.
The disabled DEBUG BoardFrameImageView path still has no readiness publisher; it is not validated by this live-renderer change.

Changing layout during an already-running initial countdown does not trigger rearm because routineStartedAt is set. This is an explicit first-start-only scope limit; it does not guarantee readiness of a replacement orientation host at expiry.
testAssessment: New stale-request test is relevant. Existing dictionary/gate tests do not replace actual scene/host lifecycle checks. This worker executed no tests.
conclusion: After the one-line field correction, no additional definite normal-route logic blocker found in task-side, opacity grouping, audio or cancellation review. Model identity should be included for a complete preparation identity. Runtime correctness and repair remain unproven.
